answer: A credit-network protocol mitigates Sybil attacks by bounding capacity across an interaction graph. Verified trust flows through bilateral channels extending like a vine between bonded peers. Verifiers evaluate max-flow cuts, rejecting identities whose routed credit drops below an acceptance ledge. An attacker seeking to harbor duplicate agents incurs the verifiable cost of locking scarce capital in channel escrows. However, collateral demands disadvantage underfunded honest participants.
